preserved_conflicts: Cover care census prints 1248, after 1092 on the SR194 cover. Page 8 prints a census for seven provinces: Nord-Kivu 679 in beds (plus 261 in health facilities without treatment centre status, which the page does not say are included), Ituri 395, Haut-Uele 77, Bas-Uele 48, Nord-Ubangi 29, Tshopo 14 and Sud-Ubangi 4, which sum to 1246 as printed (1507 with the 261). The cover figure is reached only by taking the Sud-Ubangi site split (2 + 4 = 6) in place of its printed census of 4, which would be a correction. The national census is withheld and no replacement is derived.

Cover prints 369 samples analysed and 68 positive with a positivity of 13.5%; 68/369 is 18.43%, which rounds and truncates to 18.4%, so the printed rate is withheld; the counts are kept. 68 equals the 68 new cases. The provincial laboratory paragraphs print 193 analysed in Nord-Kivu, 107 in Ituri, 9 in Tshopo, 9 in Nord-Ubangi and 11 in Bas-Uele (329), and 40 received in Haut-Uele; they sum to 369 only with the Haut-Uele samples received counted as analysed. The printed positives (Ituri 15, Haut-Uele 6, Tshopo, Nord-Ubangi and Bas-Uele 0) do not reach 68 without Nord-Kivu, which prints approximate counts only.

Nord-Kivu laboratory prints 193 samples analysed, broken down as 111 new, 25 repeat and 56 post-mortem samples (192), with positivity by type (14%, 32%, 34%) and positives given as "about 16", 8 and "about 19"; the rates and approximate counts are withheld.

Laboratory positives differ from Table 1 new cases: Ituri 15 positives against 20 new cases, Haut-Uele 6 against 9, and Tshopo 9 samples all negative against 3 new cases. Table 1 is kept; the laboratory counts are kept as printed.

Nord-Kivu care prints 679 patients in beds (152 confirmed, 527 suspects) and, separately, 261 in health facilities without treatment centre status (SR194 counted these inside its 601). It prints 161 admissions and 839 exits including 9 deaths, 64 non-cases and 830 cumulative recoveries; 839 is 9 + 830, not a day count, and 9 + 64 + 830 = 903. The exit total is withheld and no daily recovery count is carried. From SR194, 601 + 161 = 762, which closes with neither 679 nor 940. The 9 deaths differ from the 7 Nord-Kivu intra-CTE deaths in Table 2 (Table 2 is kept).

Haut-Uele care prints 77 patients (45 confirmed) after 19 admissions (5 confirmed) and 12 exits, with 1 death printed separately. From the SR194 census of 74 (27 confirmed), 74 + 19 - 12 = 81 (80 with the death as a further exit), and the confirmed count can reach at most 32, against 77 and 45 printed. The census and split are kept as printed.

Sud-Ubangi care prints 4 suspects in beds and splits them as 2 and 4 at two sites (6); the census is withheld. It prints an occupancy of 10% with no bed count in this edition; 10% of the 60 beds SR194 printed is 6, not 4, so the 10% occupancy is withheld. The cumulative of 53 people registered has parts summing to 56 (2 confirmed, 6 pending, 48 non-cases), and the days without a confirmed case move from 53 (SR194) to 55 in one day; neither is promoted.

Bas-Uele care prints 48 suspects in isolation after 4 exits and no printed admission; from the SR194 census of 22, 22 - 4 = 18. Tshopo prints 14 patients (5 confirmed) after 6 suspects in SR194 with no admission or exit printed. Nord-Ubangi prints 29 patients after 28, with the cumulative since opening (91 admissions) repeated from SR194, which now gives 28. All three censuses are kept as printed.

Table 3: the Bas-Uele row repeats the SR194 row in every cell (123 living and 3 deceased, 126 alerts, 14 and 2 validated, 109 and 1 invalidated, 16 investigated, 0 transferred). It is kept as printed because the printed totals include it, and is not read as new activity.

Nord-Ubangi has no Table 5 column in this edition; Bas-Uele and Sud-Ubangi return after none in SR194.

Nord-Kivu (432 to 434 notified), Sud-Kivu (29 to 30), Tshopo (33 to 40 notified) and Haut-Uele (19 to 20 notified, 15 to 16 validated) move in agreement with their day cells. Burial and IPC counts are not promoted: Nord-Kivu prints 52 burials of 77 death alerts with 1 body swabbed; Ituri 48 burials of 74 alerts (64.9%), 9 bodies swabbed and 17 failures (23%); Haut-Uele 6 burials and 5 bodies swabbed; Tshopo 7 death alerts with a burial completion rate of 66%; Sud-Ubangi no burial on the day and a cumulative of 8.

Single-patient details in the PoE/PoC, vaccination, care, IPC and laboratory paragraphs (one suspect intercepted, with the names of the control point and the receiving treatment centre, one suspect referred, with the name of another control point, one serious adverse event with clinical details, numbered cases whose households were decontaminated, named facilities and named treatment products) are not carried beyond the counts above.

No province printed a dose stock in SR194, so no stock is checked across editions; each printed stock closes within this edition.

Recoveries: the cover prints 17 recoveries; the care page prints a day count only for Ituri (8). Nord-Kivu prints 830 cumulative recoveries inside its exit line, and Haut-Uele 12 exits without a breakdown. The cover figure is kept; it is not reconciled with the care page.

Repeats: the security section repeats SR194 verbatim and is printed under a Nord-Kivu heading while describing control points in Sud-Kivu and Haut-Uele; the Bas-Uele treatment centre construction at 60% restates SR190 to SR194; the Haut-Uele meal counts (74 patients, 88 front-line staff, 64 carers) and CREC counts (95 talks, 4 home visits, 160 sessions) repeat SR194. None is promoted as a new SR195 event.

Single-patient details in the PoE/PoC, vaccination, care, IPC and laboratory paragraphs (one suspect intercepted, with the names of the control point and the receiving treatment centre, one suspect referred, with the name of another control point, one serious adverse event with clinical details, numbered cases whose households were decontaminated, named facilities and named treatment products) are not carried beyond the counts above.

Recoveries: the 17 recoveries on the cover cannot be checked against the care page. Only Ituri prints a day count (8 recovered); Nord-Kivu prints 830 cumulative recoveries and no day count, Haut-Uele prints 12 exits without a breakdown, and no other province prints a recovery on the day. Provincial cumulative recoveries are not promoted.

Vaccination: Ituri prints no vaccination line in this edition (SR194 printed a protocol line with no count); no row is created. The Nord-Kivu and Tshopo rows count people and the Haut-Uele row counts doses; they are not summed. No page names a vaccine product, and no vaccine is licensed for Bundibugyo virus disease.

challenges.finding: Publisher reports persistent insecurity keeping some Ituri control points inactive and two of 15 Ituri laboratories suspended (13 functioning, 86.7%); one Nord-Kivu control point non-functional after a security incident; only 3 of 13 Haut-Uele laboratories functioning (23%); community resistance in one Haut-Uele zone hindering rings and decontamination, and burial failures attributed to community resistance; 17 failed burials in Ituri (23% of 74 death alerts); in Sud-Ubangi too few IPC-trained staff, missing IPC kits, no triage areas at facility entrances and non-compliant waste areas; IPC gaps found in three assessed Ituri facilities; continuing nutrient needs for specific diets in Haut-Uele (also reported in SR194); and 2 Bas-Uele suspects leaving isolation without authorisation before a laboratory result. The security section repeats SR194 verbatim (missing isolation equipment and basic material at several Sud-Kivu control points; no formal sanitary barriers at some Haut-Uele control points). IPC counts: Nord-Kivu 23 of 36 planned rings opened (63.9%), 19 of 25 health facilities (76%) and 16 of 38 households (42.1%) decontaminated; Ituri 10 of 18 rings, 12 of 17 households and 7 of 7 facilities; Haut-Uele a ring opening rate of 100% in 6 zones; Tshopo 75 of 117 facilities with IPC kits (64.1%). No intervention effect is established.

Contact follow-up covers five provinces reporting a cohort. Sud-Ubangi prints ND and the Bas-Uele zero is withheld after the contact cohort moved between province labels in earlier editions. The lowest printed rate is Nord-Kivu (67.8%). The national rate falls from 85.1% to 82.1% while the cohort grows from 35 105 to 46 424 (Ituri from 16 529 to 27 955), so no same-cohort trend is inferred. No zero follow-up is inferred for any province.

vaccination_by_province.scope_note: Nord-Kivu counts people vaccinated: 6 019 in cumulative (3 280 men, 2 739 women) across 7 reporting zones, 620 of them contacts. Dose stock as printed: 7 500 received, 6 019 used, 1 480 remaining and 1 lost (6 019 + 1 480 + 1 = 7 500). SR194 printed 5 342 people (unchanged from SR193) and no stock; no daily count is printed, so no daily value is derived and the rise is not promoted as a day figure. No coverage or denominator is printed. One serious adverse event following immunisation is reported; single-patient details are not carried and no cumulative adverse event count is printed. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations or quantities; there is no national total. The SitRep does not name the vaccine product.

Tshopo counts people vaccinated (15 617 in cumulative, 6 307 of them women, 40.4%). INSP prints a provincial coverage of 104.4% without printing a denominator in this edition, and none is carried; the reference group behind the rate is not printed, so a rate above 100% cannot be read against a population. Dose stock as printed: 15 900 received, 15 617 administered (98.2%) and 283 remaining (15 900 - 15 617 = 283). SR194 printed 15 228 people and no stock; no daily count is printed, so no daily value is derived. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations or quantities; there is no national total. The SitRep does not name the vaccine product.

Haut-Uele prints doses, not people, in this edition: 6 100 received, 5 097 used and 1 003 remaining (6 100 - 5 097 = 1 003), across the eligible zones. The printed coverage of 84% matches doses used over doses received (83.6%), not people over a denominator, and is withheld; no denominator is printed. SR194 printed 4 740 people vaccinated of 5 693 pre-registered and no stock; doses and people are different units, so no change is derived. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations or quantities; there is no national total. The SitRep does not name the vaccine product.

care_continuity: The printed national care census (1248) is withheld because it does not reconcile with the seven provinces that print a census in SR195, which sum to 1246; provincial censuses and patient-status splits are incomplete.

Nord-Kivu: 679 patients in beds (152 confirmed + 527 suspects), 75 of them children under 5 (11%) and 25 critical; in addition 261 patients (3 confirmed, 258 suspects) are cared for in health facilities without treatment centre status. SR194 counted the patients outside treatment centres inside its 601; this edition does not say whether the 679 includes the 261, so 679 is kept as printed and the 261 is not added. The 9 deaths and 64 non-cases of the day are kept as day counts from the exit sentence; its 839 total is withheld because it adds 830 cumulative recoveries. The census does not close against SR194 either way (601 + 161 admissions = 762; 679 would need 83 exits and 940 would need more admissions than printed). No occupancy or bed count is printed. National care census withheld for this edition (the cover figure conflicts with the provincial censuses).

Ituri: 395 patients (138 confirmed + 257 suspects), 25 critical, after 113 admissions (all suspects) and 53 exits (8 recovered, 31 non-cases, 9 deaths of which 6 confirmed, and 5 exits without medical advice). Hot meals are reported for 359 of 377 patients, a base that differs from the census; not promoted. The ambulance fleet is printed as 43 vehicles (36 operational, 7 out of service). National care census withheld for this edition (the cover figure conflicts with the provincial censuses).

Haut-Uele: 77 patients (45 confirmed + 32 suspects) after 19 admissions (5 confirmed, 14 suspects) and 12 exits (not broken down), with 1 death in a treatment centre printed separately, in agreement with Table 2. The census does not close against SR194: 74 + 19 - 12 = 81, or 80 with the death as a further exit, against 77 printed; and from 27 confirmed in SR194, 5 confirmed admissions give at most 32, against 45 printed. Kept as printed. Occupancy is printed as 44% (49% of suspect beds, 39% of confirmed beds) with no bed count; kept as printed. National care census withheld for this edition (the cover figure conflicts with the provincial censuses).

Nord-Ubangi: 29 patients across two sites (12 and 17), 4 of them children under 5. No admission or exit is printed. The printed cumulative since the sites opened (91 admissions: 8 confirmed, 1 death, 7 recovered, 1 other exit, 54 non-cases) repeats SR194 and now gives 28, against 29 printed; it is not promoted. The printed intra-CTE CFR of 12.5% is 1 death among 8 confirmed. No occupancy and no confirmed or suspect split is printed. National care census withheld for this edition (the cover figure conflicts with the provincial censuses).

Bas-Uele: No confirmed patient hospitalised; 48 suspects in isolation in health facilities, with 4 exits (2 non-cases after laboratory testing and 2 who left without authorisation after clinical improvement, before a laboratory result). No admission is printed. The census does not close against SR194: 22 - 4 = 18, against 48 printed. Kept as printed. National care census withheld for this edition (the cover figure conflicts with the provincial censuses).

Tshopo: 14 patients (5 confirmed + 9 suspects), after 6 suspects and no confirmed patient in SR194; no admission or exit is printed. Kept as printed. Table 2 prints 3 new Tshopo cases. Cumulative treatment and post-exposure prophylaxis counts are printed and not promoted (the prophylaxis parts sum to 748 against 753 printed). National care census withheld for this edition (the cover figure conflicts with the provincial censuses).

Sud-Ubangi: No confirmed patient hospitalised. The census is printed as 4 suspects in beds, while the same sentence splits them as 2 and 4 at two sites (6); the census and suspect count are withheld. The printed occupancy of 10% has no bed count in this edition (10% of the 60 beds SR194 printed is 6, the site split, not 4) and is withheld. The province prints 55 days without a confirmed case (53 in SR194, one day earlier) and a cumulative of 53 people registered whose parts sum to 56; neither is promoted. National care census withheld for this edition (the cover figure conflicts with the provincial censuses).
